original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-RHom-into-K-injective}
Let $(\mathcal{C}, \mathcal{O})$ be a ringed site. Let $L$ and $M$
be objects of $D(\mathcal{O})$. Let $\mathcal{I}^\bullet$
be a K-injective complex of $\mathcal{O}$-modules representing $M$. Let
$\mathcal{L}^\bullet$ be a complex of $\mathcal{O}$-modules
representing $L$.
Then
$$
H^0(\Gamma(U, \SheafHom^\bullet(\mathcal{L}^\bullet, \mathcal{I}^\bullet))) =
\Hom_{D(\mathcal{O}_U)}(L|_U, M|_U)
$$
for all $U \in \Ob(\mathcal{C})$. Similarly,
$H^0(\Gamma(\mathcal{C},
\SheafHom^\bullet(\mathcal{L}^\bullet, \mathcal{I}^\bullet))) =
\Hom_{D(\mathcal{O})}(L, M)$.

final_content.statement:
For a ringed site (C,O), SheafHom^bullet(L^bullet,M^bullet) is the internal **complex** of O-module sheaves: its degree n term is the product over p+q=n of SheafHom_O(L^{-q},M^p), with graded differential d(f)=d_M∘f−(−1)^n f∘d_L (source lines 8574–8595). Tot is the ordinary total tensor-product complex with Koszul signs. This is defined on unbounded complexes, and is distinct from the derived internal Hom RSheafHom.

L,M∈D(O), L^bullet represents L, and I^bullet represents M and is K-injective.
conclusions: If L,M are objects of D(O), L^bullet represents L and I^bullet is a K-injective representative of M, then for every site object U, H^0 Γ(U,SheafHom^bullet(L^bullet,I^bullet))≅Hom_{D(O_U)}(L|_U,M|_U); also the corresponding global H^0 gives Hom_{D(O)}(L,M).

semantic_review_note: For derived objects L,M, any representative L• and K-injective representative I• of M yield H⁰ of sections of the sheaf internal Hom complex equal to Hom in derived category after restriction to U, as well as globally. The K-injectivity is required only of target representative.

original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-RHom-from-K-flat-into-K-injective}
Let $(\mathcal{C}, \mathcal{O})$ be a ringed site. Let $\mathcal{I}^\bullet$
be a K-injective complex of $\mathcal{O}$-modules. Let
$\mathcal{L}^\bullet$ be a K-flat complex of $\mathcal{O}$-modules.
Then $\SheafHom^\bullet(\mathcal{L}^\bullet, \mathcal{I}^\bullet)$
is a K-injective complex of $\mathcal{O}$-modules.
